tour.title: Repository and Three Projects
tour.description: Start with the README to understand why this fork replaces the remote game catalogue with local Steam metadata. The solution contains two Windows executables, SAM.Picker and SAM.Game, sharing SAM.API; the scanner belongs to the picker rather than a fourth project.

tour.title: Picker Startup
tour.description: SAM.Picker checks that it is not being run from the Steam installation directory, creates API.Client, and initializes it with app ID zero before starting the GamePicker message loop. A running, accessible Steam session is therefore required before local discovery begins; the scanner override does not replace native client initialization.

tour.title: Shared Native Steam Session
tour.description: Client.Initialize loads Steam, creates a pipe, connects the global Steam user, and obtains the versioned interface wrappers needed by both executables. Steam.GetInstallPath reads the machine registry, while Steam.Load resolves steamclient.dll exports; this path is independent of the scanner root search.

tour.title: Versioned Native Wrappers
tour.description: NativeWrapper attaches managed wrappers to Steam native function tables and caches marshalled delegates. SteamClient018 uses that mechanism to obtain the app, user, statistics, and utilities interfaces used by the startup sequence; the Interfaces directory supplies the native layout contracts.
tour.languageLesson: C# generics and delegates let one NativeWrapper implementation attach different typed vtable layouts while marshalling native function pointers into callable managed delegates.

tour.title: Discover Local Steam Libraries
tour.description: SteamLibraryScanner finds a Steam root from SAM_STEAM_PATH, registry candidates, or Program Files, includes its primary library, and reads steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf for additional libraries. It supports both numeric path strings and newer nested path entries, scans appmanifest_*.acf, deduplicates app IDs, and returns sorted candidate names. Manifest presence defines candidates: it does not validate StateFlags, the installation directory, or achievement support.

tour.title: Background Scan to UI
tour.description: The GamePicker constructor initializes the controls and callback subscription, then AddGames clears the collection and starts the list BackgroundWorker. Its DoWork method scans files; completion returns to the UI thread to add candidates, rebuild the filtered list, enable refresh, and begin image work. The virtual ListView requests visible item records from _FilteredGames instead of eagerly constructing every row.
tour.languageLesson: Windows Forms BackgroundWorker separates file I/O from UI updates: DoWork runs off the UI thread, while RunWorkerCompleted marshals completion back to the creating synchronization context.

tour.title: Subscription Names and Filtering
tour.description: Each discovered app passes SteamApps008.IsSubscribedApp before it enters the picker collection. SteamApps001 supplies the preferred cached name and image metadata, with the local manifest name used as fallback; GameInfo supplies the final app-ID fallback. RefreshGames applies search and type filters to these admitted games, so the displayed set can be smaller than the manifest inventory.

tour.title: Callbacks and Optional Images
tour.description: The picker timer pumps Client.RunCallbacks and dispatches app-data changes to the registered callback, which refreshes known-game metadata and image work. Visible rows lazily queue logos using localized capsule metadata or a logo fallback. Candidate discovery no longer downloads the remote catalogue, but artwork can still be downloaded from Steam CDN URLs.

tour.title: Open the Game Editor
tour.description: Activating a picker row starts SAM.Game.exe with its app ID as a command-line argument; the processes share code through SAM.API rather than a live Client instance. SAM.Game initializes its own client for that nonzero app ID and opens Manager, whose constructor requests user statistics. Starting SAM.Game without arguments redirects to SAM.Picker.

tour.title: Load Binary Stat Schemas
tour.description: After successful user-stat retrieval, Manager reads appcache/stats/UserGameStatsSchema_<appId>.bin to construct statistic and achievement definitions. KeyValue and StreamHelpers parse this binary cache, while UserStatType distinguishes integer, float, rate, and achievement definitions. This parser is separate from the text KeyValues reader used for libraryfolders.vdf and ACF manifests.

tour.title: Typed Editor Data
tour.description: Schema definitions describe available statistics, while editable StatInfo records retain values and modification state for the editor grid. AchievementInfo couples achievement state, permissions, display data, and ListView imagery. These models support permission-aware editing after discovery has handed off to the per-game editor.

tour.title: Retrieve and Store Statistics
tour.description: SteamUserStats013 provides the native reads, writes, resets, and asynchronous user-stat requests used by Manager. The UserStatsReceived callback delivers completion so Manager can load the schema and populate the editor; store actions apply changed achievements and statistics before StoreStats persists them. The shared callback dispatcher is therefore used for both picker metadata updates and editor statistics.

tour.title: Build and Package Windows Apps
tour.description: The three SDK-style projects target .NET Framework 4.8 with x86 configuration and C# 9, with both executables referencing SAM.API. The AppVeyor pipeline restores and builds the solution, patches version metadata, and packages release executables and DLLs. These settings explain the native Steam interop and shared-output deployment assumptions behind the preceding runtime flow.
